grammar.form: 動詞[どうし]の活用[かつよう] · Verb Conjugation
grammar.tag: Three verb groups: ru-verbs, u-verbs, irregular
def: Japanese verbs fall into three conjugation groups. Ru-verbs end in -eru/-iru and simply swap る for ます／ません. U-verbs end in a consonant+u and swap u for います／いません. する and 来[く]る are irregular. Watch out for verbs like 帰[かえ]る that look like ru-verbs but actually conjugate as u-verbs.
ex: 食[た]べる → 食[た]べます／食[た]べません (ru-verb)
飲[の]む → 飲[の]みます／飲[の]みません (u-verb)
帰[かえ]る → 帰[かえ]ります／帰[かえ]りません (u-verb, despite the -eru ending)

grammar.form: 動詞[どうし]と「現在形[げんざいけい]」 · Verb Types and "Present Tense"
def: The Japanese present tense of action verbs covers two English meanings: something you do habitually, or something you will do / plan to do in the future.
ex: 私[わたし]はよくテレビを見[み]ます。 (I often watch TV. — habitual)
私[わたし]はあした京都[きょうと]に行[い]きます。 (I will go to Kyoto tomorrow. — future)

grammar.form: 助詞[じょし] を・で・に・へ · Particles
grammar.tag: Object, place of action, goal/time, direction
def: を marks the direct object of a verb. で marks where an action takes place. に marks the goal of movement (行[い]く/来[く]る/帰[かえ]る) or a specific point in time. へ can replace に for the goal of movement, but never for time.
ex: コーヒーを飲[の]みます。 (I drink coffee.)
図書館[としょかん]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。 (I will read books at the library.)
うちに／へ帰[かえ]ります。 (I will return home.)

grammar.form: 時[とき]の表[あらわ]し方[かた] · Time References
grammar.tag: When に is required, and when it's dropped
def: Use に with days of the week and numerical time expressions ("on Sunday," "at 10:45"). Don't use に with relative time words (today, tomorrow), regular intervals (every day), or the word "when." Parts of the day and "weekend" can go either way.
ex: 日曜日[にちようび]に 行[い]きます。 (I will go on Sunday.)
あした 来[き]ます。 (I will come tomorrow — no に.)
週末[しゅうまつ]（に）何[なに]をしますか。 (What will you do on the weekend? — に optional)

def: ませんか (the present negative + question particle) invites someone to do something together. Its affirmative counterpart ますか can only be read as a plain question, never an invitation.
ex: 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べませんか。 (Would you like to have lunch with me?)
テニスをしませんか。 (Will you play tennis with me?)

grammar.form: 頻度[ひんど]の副詞[ふくし] · Frequency Adverbs
grammar.tag: 毎日[まいにち]・よく・ときどき・あまり・ぜんぜん
def: Frequency adverbs describe how often something happens. あまり (not often) and ぜんぜん (not at all) anticipate a negative ending, so the sentence must end in ～ません.
ex: 私[わたし]はときどき図書館[としょかん]に行[い]きます。 (I sometimes go to a library.)
たけしさんはあまり勉強[べんきょう]しません。 (Takeshi doesn't study much.)

grammar.form: 語順[ごじゅん] · Word Order
def: Japanese word order is flexible since particles, not position, mark grammatical roles — but a typical sentence lines up as topic, time, place, object, then the verb or adjective at the end.
ex: 私[わたし]は 今日[きょう] 図書館[としょかん]で 日本語[にほんご]を 勉強[べんきょう]します。 (I will study Japanese in the library today.)

grammar.form: とりたて助詞[じょし] は · The Topic Particle は
grammar.tag: Broaching a topic — not always the subject
def: は marks the topic of the sentence — what you want to talk about — which is often, but not always, the grammatical subject. A topic can even be the direct object of the sentence, as in 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]は？ where 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん] (dinner) is what's eaten, not who eats it.
ex: 週末[しゅうまつ]は たいてい何[なに]をしますか。 (As for the weekend, what do you usually do?)
晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]は？／食[た]べません。 (How about dinner? / I will not eat [it].)
